Abstract Summary: Attention Is All You Need

Title: Attention Is All You Need
Authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Lukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin

Key Points:
- The paper introduces the Transformer, a neural sequence transduction architecture based entirely on attention mechanisms, removing recurrence and convolution.
- Its central innovation is self-attention, which allows the model to capture dependencies between tokens regardless of distance while enabling much greater parallelization during training.
- The architecture uses an encoder-decoder design with stacked layers, multi-head self-attention, residual connections, layer normalization, and position-wise feed-forward networks.
- Scaled dot-product attention improves efficiency and stability, while multi-head attention helps the model attend to different representation subspaces simultaneously.
- Because the model has no recurrence or convolution, positional encodings are added to token embeddings to preserve sequence order information.
- Compared with recurrent and convolutional models, self-attention reduces sequential operations and shortens path lengths between distant positions, improving the modeling of long-range dependencies.
- On WMT 2014 English-to-German translation, the Transformer (big) achieved 28.4 BLEU, outperforming previous best results by more than 2 BLEU.
- On WMT 2014 English-to-French translation, it achieved 41.0 BLEU with substantially lower training cost than prior state-of-the-art systems.
- The paper demonstrates that attention-only architectures can outperform traditional RNN- and CNN-based approaches in machine translation while training faster.
- The work laid the foundation for many later advances in natural language processing and large language models.

Concise Abstract:
This paper presents the Transformer, a sequence transduction model built entirely on attention mechanisms. By replacing recurrence and convolution with self-attention and multi-head attention, the model enables greater parallelization, captures long-range dependencies more effectively, and reduces training cost. Experimental results on major machine translation benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, establishing the Transformer as a highly effective architecture for language modeling and translation tasks.
